globalconfigurationinfo-text: Note: Global configuration options with .wslconfig are only available for distributions running as WSL 2 in Windows Build 19041 and later. Changes take effect after WSL restarts.
absolutewindowspath-text: An absolute Windows path to a custom Linux kernel. Backslashes have to be doubled, e.g. C:\\kernel\\vmlinux.
memoryinfo-text: How much memory to assign to the WSL 2 VM. Default: 50% of the total memory on Windows. A plain number is bytes; add MB or GB for other units, e.g. 8GB.
processorinfo-text: How many logical processors to assign to the WSL 2 VM. Default: the same number of logical processors Windows has.
wildcardinfo-text: Whether ports bound to wildcard or localhost inside the instance can be reached from Windows via localhost:port. Default: on.
swapinfo-text: How much swap space to add to the WSL 2 VM, 0 for no swap file. Swap storage is disk-based RAM used when memory demand exceeds limit on hardware device. Default: 25% of the memory on Windows, rounded up to the nearest GB. (e.g. 8GB, 512MB)
vhdinfo-text: An absolute Windows path to the swap virtual hard disk. Default: %Temp%\swap.vhdx.
guiinfo-text: Boolean to turn on or off support for GUI applications (WSLg) in WSL. Default: on.
consoleinfo-text: Boolean to turn on an output console window that shows the contents of dmesg upon start of a WSL 2 distro instance. Default: off. Only available for Windows 11.
nestedvirtinfo-text: Boolean to turn on or off nested virtualization, enabling other nested VMs to run inside WSL 2. Default: on. Only available for Windows 11.
vmidleinfo-text: The number of milliseconds that a VM is idle, before it is shut down. Default: 60000. Only available for Windows 11.
report-text: Do you want to upload the log file or open a GitHub issue?
languagechange-text: The language changes straight away. Save to keep it.
cleanupbody-text: Do you really want to clean up the distribution? This will compact the virtual hard disk to reclaim space. The instance will be stopped and unavailable during this process.
movebody-text: Do you really want to move the distribution %s0 to the default distro path? This will export and re-import the distribution. This may take some time.
savesatemplatequestion-text: Do you want to save %s as a template?
saveastemplatebody-text: This will result in shutting down the instance and exporting it. This process can take some time, during which the instance will not be usable.

mountoptionshint-text: Filesystem mount options, e.g. data=ordered. WSL does not accept generic options like ro or rw here.

mountshostinvalid-text: The folder must be an absolute path without quotes.
mountsguestrequired-text: Enter the path inside the instance.
mountsguestinvalid-text: The path inside the instance must be absolute, use only letters, digits, . _ - and must not be a system directory such as /etc or /usr.
mountsguestduplicate-text: %s is already used by another shared folder.
mountsnextstart-text: Changes take effect the next time the VM starts.
mountsownerhint-text: Inside the VM the files keep this Mac's ownership: root has full access, other accounts get the folder's permissions.
mountsrestart-text: Shared folders of '%s' saved. Restart it to mount them.
mountsonstart-text: Shared folders of '%s' saved. They are mounted when it starts.
mountsfailed-text: Could not update the shared folders of '%s'.
mountsunreachable-text: The instance could not be reached to read its shared folders.
mountswritefailed-text: Could not write /etc/fstab inside the instance.
mountsapplywarning-text: Saved to /etc/fstab, but mounting right away failed: %s
mountsguestproblem-text: The VM reported a problem with its shared folders
mountsapplyfailed-text: Saved to /etc/fstab, but mounting right away failed.
mountsfstabdisabled-text: This instance has mountFsTab disabled in /etc/wsl.conf, so its shared folders are not mounted automatically when it starts.
mountsunsupported-text: Shared folders are not available for this instance backend.
ai-workspace-mounts-subtitle: Give the workspace tools access to project folders on this computer.
diskofflinehint-text: Hint: The disk might be online in Windows. Set it to Offline in Disk Management and try again.
unknownmounterror-text: Unknown error occurred during mount operation.
kernelmodulesinfo-text: An absolute Windows path to a custom Linux kernel modules VHD.
safemodeinfo-text: Run WSL in "Safe Mode" which disables many features and is intended to be used to recover distributions that are in bad states. Only available for Windows 11 and WSL version 0.66.2+.
maxcrashdumpcountinfo-text: Set the maximum number of crash dump files that will be retained. Default: 10.
dnsproxyinfo-text: Configure the DNS server in Linux to the NAT on the host. Default: on. Only applicable when the networking mode is nat; turning it off mirrors the DNS servers from Windows to Linux instead.
networkingmodeinfo-text: How WSL connects to the network: none, nat, bridged, mirrored or virtioproxy. Default: nat, which an unrecognised value also falls back to. bridged has been deprecated since WSL 2.4.5.
firewallinfo-text: Allow Windows Firewall rules to filter WSL network traffic, including the Hyper-V traffic of the WSL 2 VM. Default: on.
dnstunnelinginfo-text: Changes how DNS requests are proxied from WSL to Windows. Default: on.
autoproxyinfo-text: Enforces WSL to use Windows' HTTP proxy information. Default: on. Only available for Windows 11.
defaultvhdsizeinfo-text: Limit the maximum size a distribution file system is allowed to take up. Default: 1099511627776 (1 TB). A plain number is bytes; add MB, GB or TB for other units.
automemoryreclaiminfo-text: How WSL gives unused memory back to Windows: disabled, gradual or dropCache. Default: dropCache, which an unrecognised value also falls back to.
sparsevhdinfo-text: When set to true, any newly created VHD will be set to sparse automatically. Default: off.
besteffortdnsparsinginfo-text: Attempt to resolve DNS requests ignoring unknown records. Default: off. Only applicable when dnsTunneling is set to true.
dnstunnelingipaddressinfo-text: Specifies the nameserver for DNS tunneling. Default: 10.255.255.254. Only applicable when dnsTunneling is set to true.
initialautoproxytimeoutinfo-text: How long, in milliseconds, to wait for the HTTP proxy information before starting the distro. Default: 1000. Only applicable when autoProxy is set to true, and the WSL instance has to be restarted to use the retrieved proxy settings.
ignoredportsinfo-text: Ports Linux applications can bind to even if they are used in Windows, as a comma-separated list, e.g. 3000,9000,9090. Only applicable when the networking mode is mirrored.
hostaddressloopbackinfo-text: Allow the container to connect to the host by its assigned IP address. Default: off. Only IPv4 addresses assigned to the host are supported. Only applicable when the networking mode is mirrored.
byok-info-text: AI Chat runs on credentials you bring: your own OpenAI-compatible API key. The AI Workspace tools (OpenCode, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent) use the same endpoint, key and model, so you set them once here.
byok-pro-required-text: Bring Your Own Key is a Pro feature.
ai-enabled-info-text: Show the AI assistant, the error diagnosis and the AI Workspace. Switched off, nothing AI-related is shown and no workspace environment is set up for you.
ai-consent-text: WSL Manager can show an AI assistant, explain errors for you and set up an AI Workspace environment. All of it is optional, and none of it runs until you say yes. You can change this any time in Settings under Bring Your Own AI Key.
ai-disabled-text: AI features are switched off. Turn them back on in Settings under Bring Your Own AI Key.
byok-apikey-hint-text: Stored locally on this device only.
byok-required-text: AI Chat needs your own API key. Add it in Settings under 'Bring Your Own AI Key'.
store-buy-info-text: One-time purchase, no subscription. Open source forever.
store-buy-detail-text: Buy once on the Microsoft Store and unlock all Pro features — AI Workspace, AI Chat (with your own API key), MCP server, and more. No subscription, free updates.
store-buy-btn: Get it on the Microsoft Store
ai-assistant-hint: Ask anything about WSL — configuration, errors, commands.
ai-error-text: The AI request failed. Please try again.
ai-run-snippet-missing-text: This run was saved as snippet %s, which has since been deleted.
backupsettingsinfo-text: Back every instance up to a folder you choose, and restore them from that folder on another PC.
backupinfo-text: Writes every selected instance to one folder as an archive, next to a small file recording which archive belongs to which instance. Copy the folder to another PC and restore it there.
backupshutdown-text: Each instance is stopped before it is exported and can be used again once its turn is over.
restoreinfo-text: Pick a folder a backup was written to. Every archive in it is imported under the name it had; instances that already exist here are left alone.
restorenomanifest-title: No backup list in this folder
restorenomanifest-text: The names come from the file names, so an instance may come back under a slightly different one.
restoreforeign-text: This backup was made by the %s backend, whose archives may not import here.
backupskipped-text: %s were already here and were left alone.
backupstopped-text: Stopped. Everything that finished before that is complete.
backupremote-title: Not available for a remote host
backupremote-text: The archives would be written on the remote machine, not in the folder you pick here. Run the app on that machine to back its instances up.
beta-info-text: This is new and still in beta. It works, but expect rough edges — feedback and bug reports on GitHub are very welcome.
mcp-info-text: Expose your WSL distros to AI agents (Claude Desktop and other MCP-compatible tools) so they can list distros, run commands, and stop distros directly — like a terminal, but for your agent. Runs locally on this machine only.
mcp-pro-required-text: The WSL MCP server is a Pro feature.
mcp-toggle-hint-text: Starts a local server your MCP client can connect to. Only reachable from this machine, and only with the token below.
mcp-tunnel-warning-text: This exposes your MCP server (and everything it can do — including running commands) to the public internet at a temporary URL. Only your access token protects it. Treat that token like a password, and only enable this if you trust whoever you're sharing the URL with.
mcp-tunnel-toggle-hint-text: Creates a temporary public HTTPS URL (via Cloudflare) that forwards to your local MCP server, so a remote client can reach it too.
mcp-tunnel-connecting-text: Setting up the tunnel… this may download a small helper the first time.
remote-wsl-over-ssh-info-text: When enabled, WSL CLI commands are sent through SSH to a remote host.
remote-wsl-target-required-text: Remote WSL is enabled, but the SSH target is missing or invalid. Use format user@host or host.
ai-workspace-subtitle: Manage AI tools and services in an isolated WSL environment
ai-workspace-pro-required-text: AI Workspace is a Pro feature. Upgrade to run Hermes Agent, OpenClaw, and Open WebUI in their own isolated environment.
ai-workspace-preparing-text: Setting up the AI workspace environment (this may take a few minutes)...
ai-workspace-docker-setup-text: Installing Docker in the AI workspace (this may take a few minutes)...
ai-workspace-docker-unavailable-text: Docker is not running in the AI workspace, so tool status could not be checked.
ai-workspace-config-schema-live-text: These fields come from the schema the installed tool describes itself with.
ai-workspace-config-schema-inferred-text: This tool publishes no schema, so the fields are the settings its config file already holds.
ai-workspace-config-schema-error-text: Its schema could not be pulled: %s
ai-workspace-config-truncated-text: Deeply nested settings are edited as raw JSON.
ai-workspace-config-missing-text: %s has no config file yet and is running on its defaults. Saving creates one.
ai-workspace-config-container-env-text: Open WebUI is configured through the environment variables its container was created with, so they are shown read-only here. Changing one means re-creating the container, which would delete everything stored in it.
ai-workspace-config-empty-text: This tool exposes no editable settings.
ai-workspace-config-load-failed-text: The configuration could not be read: %s
ai-workspace-config-save-failed-text: The configuration could not be saved: %s
ai-workspace-config-restart-hint-text: Restart %s for the new settings to take effect.
ai-workspace-uninstall-confirm: %s and everything it has stored are removed from the ai-workspace instance. This cannot be undone.
ai-workspace-dashboard-failed-text: Couldn't open the dashboard. Make sure the tool is still running and try again.
compact-nospace-text: Not enough free space to compact: the disk is %s0 but only %s1 is available. Free up space or move the instance to a larger drive.
plan-free-detail: Everything for managing WSL locally. AI features are not included.
plan-store-detail: Bought once in the Microsoft Store. All Pro features are unlocked, updates included.
selectdockerimage-text: Please select or enter a local Docker image
byok-required-note: The AI features use your own OpenAI-compatible API key. No AI service is hosted or included — you pay your provider directly, or point them at a local model.
rate-title: Getting good use out of WSL Manager?
rate-text: A rating on the Microsoft Store helps other people find the app. It takes a few seconds, and it genuinely makes a difference for a small project.
ai-workspace-startingup-hint-text: The tool is still starting up. Its dashboard opens once it is ready.
ai-workspace-install-progress-text: Installing... waiting for the first output from the installer.
defaultuserinfo-text: The default user of this distro, stored in /etc/wsl.conf. Unlike "Start user" above, this applies to every way the distro is started, not only launches from this app, and it is kept when the distro is exported.
wslconfrestart-text: Restart this distro to apply the changes
ignoredinmirrored-text: Ignored when the networking mode is mirrored.
unitexample-text: e.g. 8GB, 512MB or a plain number of bytes
bootsystemdinfo-text: Use systemd as the init system in this distro. Requires WSL 0.67.6 or newer. The default depends on the distro.
bootcommandinfo-text: A command run as root every time this distro starts, e.g. service docker start. Its output is not shown, and a failure does not stop the distro.
automountenabledinfo-text: Automatically mount the Windows drives under the mount root. Default: on.
automountmountfstabinfo-text: Mount the entries of /etc/fstab when the distro starts. Default: on.
automountrootinfo-text: The directory the Windows drives are mounted under. Default: /mnt/, so C: becomes /mnt/c.
automountoptionsinfo-text: Comma-separated DrvFs options for the Windows drives: uid, gid, umask, fmask, dmask, metadata and case. umask, fmask and dmask have no effect unless metadata is set as well. Example: metadata,uid=1000,gid=1000,umask=22
networkgeneratehostsinfo-text: Let WSL generate /etc/hosts from the Windows host. Default: on.
networkgenerateresolvconfinfo-text: Let WSL generate /etc/resolv.conf with the DNS servers of the Windows host. Turn this off to keep your own DNS configuration. Default: on.
networkhostnameinfo-text: The hostname of this distro. Defaults to the Windows computer name.
interopenabledinfo-text: Allow this distro to start Windows executables. Default: on. Requires Windows 10 1809 or newer.
interopappendwindowspathinfo-text: Append the Windows PATH to the Linux PATH so Windows programs can be called by name. Default: on.
gpuenabledinfo-text: Make the Windows GPU available inside this distro. Default: on.
usewindowstimezoneinfo-text: Keep this distro's time zone in sync with the Windows one. Default: on.
protectbinfmtinfo-text: When on, WSL keeps its own binfmt registration for Windows interop and systemd cannot replace it. Turning it off hands the registration to systemd, which can stop Windows programs from running inside this distro. Default: on. Requires Windows 11 or Server 2022.
settingoutofrange-text: Outside the supported range (%s), so it is shown as text and saved exactly as written.
settinginvalidsize-text: Not a size WSL understands. Use a plain number of bytes, or add KB, MB, GB or TB.
startuserinfo-text: Only applies to terminals this app starts. To change the user every other way of starting this distro gets, use the User setting below.
wslconfwritefailed-text: Could not write "%s" to /etc/wsl.conf. The setting was not applied.
wslinbox-text: Inbox build (does not report a version)
updatewslwebdownloadinfo-text: Downloads the update directly instead of through the Microsoft Store. Use this when the Store is blocked.
wslconfigwritefailed-text: Could not write .wslconfig. The changed settings were not saved.
requireswsl-text: Requires WSL %s or newer. These actions are not available on the installed build.
vmresourcescpudetail-text: %s across the whole virtual machine · %s processors
vmresourcesmemorydetail-text: %s of %s in use across the whole virtual machine
vmresourcesnotrunning-text: %s is not running, so it is using no processor time and no memory. Start it to watch its usage here.
vmresourcesfailed-text: Could not read what %s is using.
vmresourcesstale-text: Last reading from %s; the figures above are no longer being updated:
vmresourcesnoproc-text: The instance answered, but without the readings this needs. Only a Linux guest publishes them.
vmresourcesshared-text: One virtual machine for every distribution
vmresourcessharedbody-text: WSL runs all distributions in a single virtual machine, so the smaller totals cover every one of them together with WSL itself. The large figures count only this distribution's own processes.
diskallocatedinfo-text: Size of ext4.vhdx on the Windows drive. It grows as the distro fills up and never shrinks on its own.
diskusedinfo-text: What the distro's own file system reports. The gap to the allocated size is what can be reclaimed.
diskusageunavailable-text: The usage could not be read. The distro has to be able to start for this.
resizediskinfo-text: Grow the virtual disk. Whole numbers only, with B, MB, GB or TB - 2.5TB is not a valid size. WSL is shut down first.
resizediskinvalid-text: Not a size WSL accepts. Use a whole number with B, MB, GB or TB; decimals are not supported.
setsparseinfo-text: Makes this distro's existing disk sparse, so space freed inside it is returned to Windows. This is not the sparseVhd option in the global settings, which only affects distros created afterwards.
sparsefailed-text: The sparse setting could not be changed: %s
movenative-text: This runs wsl --manage --move, a single supported operation. The distro is never unregistered.
movelegacy-text: The installed WSL has no move command, so the distro is exported to a file, unregistered and imported again. Do not close the app while this runs.
custompackageinfo-text: Package a distro as a .wsl file, or install one. A .wsl file is a root filesystem archive plus an /etc/wsl-distribution.conf that tells Windows how to set the distro up on first launch: the out-of-box experience, the default user, the Start menu shortcut and the Windows Terminal profile.
custompackageunsupported-text: Building and installing .wsl packages needs the Microsoft Store build of WSL. Update WSL from the global settings screen.
distributionconfinfo-text: Read from and written to /etc/wsl-distribution.conf in the selected distro. The export below freezes these values into the package, so set them first.
distrounreachable-text: This distro could not be read. Start it once, or pick another one.
oobedefaultnameinfo-text: The name the distro is registered under. Required for a .wsl file to install by double-click; installing with a name overrides it.
oobecommandinfo-text: Runs the first time an interactive shell opens in the installed distro. A non-zero exit counts as failure and the user cannot open a shell, so test it before packaging.
oobedefaultuidinfo-text: The UID the distro starts as. Set it to 1000 when the first-run command creates an account, and use the same UID in both places.
writeoobescriptinfo-text: Writes Microsoft's sample account-creation script to /etc/oobe.sh, makes it executable, and points the first-run command and the default user ID at it.
shortcutenabledinfo-text: Whether installing the package adds a Start menu entry. On by default.
shortcuticoninfo-text: Path inside the distro to an .ico file of at most 10 MB. WSL's own icon is used when this is not set.
terminalprofileenabledinfo-text: Whether installing the package adds a Windows Terminal profile. On by default.
terminalprofiletemplateinfo-text: Path inside the distro to a JSON fragment used as the terminal profile. The name and command line are filled in by WSL. A default profile is generated when this is not set.
packagereadinessinfo-text: Checked against Microsoft's recommendations for a custom distribution.
packageready-text: This distro is ready to package.
packagenodefaultname-text: No default name is set, so this package cannot be installed by double-clicking it.
packageoobenotexecutable-text: The first-run command %s is not executable inside this distro. The installed distro would refuse to open a shell.
packagenooobe-text: No first-run command is set. The installed distro starts as root and never asks for a user account.
packagenouid-text: A first-run command is set but no default user ID. If the command creates an account, set both to 1000.
packageiconformat-text: The shortcut icon must be an .ico file of at most 10 MB.
packagenowslconf-text: This distro has no /etc/wsl.conf. A packaged distro should carry one, at minimum to state whether systemd starts.
packageresolvconf-text: /etc/resolv.conf is present. WSL generates this file, and shipping one bakes in DNS settings that will be wrong on other machines.
packagedistroinfo-text: Exports the whole root filesystem of the selected distro. This takes minutes and produces a file about as large as the distro; the distro is stopped first so the archive is consistent.
packageformatinfo-text: gzip is the recommended format. Other formats risk breaking compatibility with older WSL versions.
packagenopath-text: Enter a path for the package file
installfromfileinfo-text: Unlike Import, this honours the package's /etc/wsl-distribution.conf, so the new distro gets its first-run setup, its default user, its Start menu shortcut and its terminal profile.
errorenterusername-text: Please enter a username for the default user, or turn the option off.
unsavedchanges-text: This page has changes you have not saved yet. Save them before leaving?
ai-chat-pro-required-text: AI Chat is a Pro feature.
distrostoppedinfo-text: Reading the settings of %s means reading /etc/wsl.conf from inside it, which starts the distro. It stays running until you terminate it.
startandread-text: Start it and read the settings
wslerror-generic-text: The operation could not be completed.
wslerror-pathnotfound-text: WSL could not find that file or folder. Check the path and try again.
wslerror-inuse-text: Windows is still using that disk, so WSL cannot take it over.
wslerror-accessdenied-text: WSL was denied access. This step needs administrator rights.
wslerror-distronotfound-text: WSL does not know an instance by that name. Refresh the list and try again.
wslerror-alreadyexists-text: An instance with that name is already registered. Choose a different name.
wslerror-diskfull-text: There is not enough free space on the drive. Free some space and try again.
wslerror-vmplatform-text: WSL 2 needs the Virtual Machine Platform Windows feature. Turn it on in Windows features and restart the computer.
wslerror-createinstance-text: WSL could not start its virtual machine. This is usually low disk space or a stale WSL session: free some space, restart WSL and try again.
wslerror-invalidparameter-text: WSL rejected one of the values. Check the entered settings and try again.
wslerror-wslmissing-text: WSL is not installed, or its Windows components are missing. Install WSL and restart the computer.
mountfailedtitle-text: The disk could not be mounted
listfailed-text: The list of WSL instances could not be read.
listfailedhint-text: Check that WSL is installed and that no other operation is running, then try again.
listfailedremote-text: The remote WSL host %s could not be reached.
listfailedremotehint-text: Check the host name, that it is switched on and that SSH accepts your key. You can also switch back to the local WSL.
connectingtoremote-text: Connecting to the remote WSL host %s...
cleaningupinstance-text: Cleaning up %s. This might take a while...
dockerusernumber-text: This image sets its default user by ID. Pick a user name in the instance settings instead.
unknownmanifest-text: This Docker image uses a manifest format the app cannot read.
mergelayersfailed-text: The image layers could not be merged into a root filesystem. The download may be incomplete: try again.
syncdownloadfailed-text: %s could not be downloaded from the sync host.
remoteinstalltriggered-text: A WSL install was started on %s.
remoteinstallfailed-text: The WSL install on %s could not be started.
remoteconfignotsupported-text: A remote .wslconfig cannot be opened in a local editor. Change the values here in Settings and press Save.
terminalnotfoundbody-text: No supported terminal emulator was found, so no shell window can be opened. Install one, for example xterm, and try again.
commandcopied-text: The command was copied to the clipboard.
dockerexportfailed-text: The local Docker image could not be exported.
ai-workspace-load-failed-text: The AI Workspace could not be opened.
wslstartupwarnings-text: WSL printed this while checking its version:
mcp-tunnel-failed-text: The Cloudflare tunnel could not be switched.
restartwslinfo-text: Shuts the WSL 2 virtual machine down so changed settings apply the next time an instance starts.
editwslconfighint-text: Opens .wslconfig in your default text editor. Changes take effect after WSL is restarted.
stopwslhint-text: Shuts down the WSL virtual machine. Every running instance stops and unsaved work inside them is lost.
startstopservinghint-text: Serves this instance on the network so another machine running WSL Manager can download it.
downloadoverridehint-text: Downloads this instance from the machine set under Sync and replaces the local copy.
createrunning-text: Creating this instance has not finished. Leaving the page keeps it running in the background.
createkeepsrunning-text: This can take several minutes. Leaving this page will not stop it.
passwordwindowhint-text: After the install a terminal window opens so you can set this user's password.
passwordwindowopen-text: Set a password for %s in the terminal window, then close it.
createdinstancenopassword-text: The instance was created, but %s still has no password.
snippetsloadfailed-text: The community snippets could not be downloaded. Check your internet connection and try again.
snippetdownloadfailed-text: The selected snippets could not be downloaded. Nothing was added.
snippetsselectone-text: Select at least one snippet to download.
vhdpathrequired-text: Choose the .vhdx or .vhd file to mount.
unmountpathrequired-text: Enter or select the path of the disk to unmount.
snippetnamerequired-text: Enter a name for this snippet.
snippetcontentrequired-text: Enter the script this snippet should run.
stopwslbody-text: Every running instance stops at once and everything running inside them is closed. Unsaved work in those instances is lost.
regeneratetokenbody-text: Every MCP client set up with the current token stops working until you give it the new one.
tokenregenerated-text: A new token was generated. Update your MCP clients with it.
distroactionsinfo-text: These act on the instance itself, not on its settings.
deletetemplatebody-text: This deletes the saved template file. Instances you already created from it are not affected.
deletesnippetbody-text: This removes the snippet from this app. No instance is changed.
clearchatbody-text: Every message in this panel is deleted and cannot be brought back.
hostsfile-info-text: Running instances can be reached by name instead of by an address that changes on every boot. The names go into %s between two markers; everything else in that file is left alone.
hostsfilesyncinfo-text: Writing the hosts file needs administrator rights, so you are asked for them whenever an address changes.
hostsfilesuffixinfo-text: Appended to each instance's own hostname, so “ubuntu” becomes “ubuntu.wsl”. Leave it empty to use the bare name.
hostsfilewritten-text: Hostnames written to the hosts file: %s
hostsfileunchanged-text: The hosts file already matches the running instances.
hostsfilecleared-text: This app's entries were removed from the hosts file.
hostsfilefailed-text: Could not write the hosts file. %s
hostsfilenotwritten-text: The file was not changed — the permission prompt was most likely dismissed.
hostsfileunsupported-text: The hosts file can only be written for instances running on this machine.
physicalmountwarning-title: Windows loses access to this disk
physicalmountwarning-text: Mounting a physical disk needs this app to run as administrator, and Windows cannot use the disk until you unmount it here.
copyinstancewarning-text: The whole instance is copied, disk included, so this needs as much free space again and can take several minutes. The source instance is stopped first.
downloadfromrepo-desc: A ready-made Linux image from this app's catalogue
turnkeylinux-desc: A pre-configured TurnKey appliance, downloaded on demand
dockerimage-desc: Pulled from Docker Hub or another registry
localrootfsfile-desc: A rootfs archive (.tar / .tar.gz) already on this PC
localdockerimage-desc: An image already in your local Docker installation
importvhdx-desc: A WSL virtual disk (.vhdx) already on this PC
recommend-docker-template: You create a lot of Docker-based instances. Save one as a template to stamp new ones faster.
recommend-cleanup: One of your instances is over 10 GB on disk. Cleanup can compact its virtual disk.
recommend-systemd: A service that needs systemd may be failing. Enable systemd for that instance in its settings.
dockerimagecheck-text: Check the image name and tag.
moveinprogress-text: An instance is being moved. The list comes back when the move finishes.
store-price-text: US$ 9.99, one-time — your Store page shows the price in your currency.
restore-hint-text: Already bought Pro but it shows Free?
restore-found-text: Pro found — thank you for your purchase!
restore-notfound-text: No Store licence found. Pro needs the Microsoft Store build of this app.
restore-notfound-free-text: No licence found on this computer. If you bought Pro in the Microsoft Store while it was still a paid app, sign in to the Microsoft Store with the account you bought it with and check again — or use “Get help” and we will send you a key.
settinginvalidvalue-text: '%s' holds a value WSL would reject. Fix it before saving.
sync-info-text: Sync copies a whole instance between two PCs running this app on the same network: one serves it, the other downloads it. The password protects that transfer.
sizeondiskhint-text: Size of the instance's virtual disk on Windows — its high-water mark, not the space in use inside it
nosnippetshint-text: Snippets you add appear here, to run inside this instance
templatesinfo-text: A template is a saved instance image you can stamp new instances from. Save one with the archive button in a distro row on Home.
createfromtemplate-text: Create a new instance from the template '%s' with this name:
snippetrunsasroot-text: This snippet is a bash script that runs as root inside the instance you pick.
snippetenvbody-text: This snippet needs a few values. They are set as environment variables for this run only, not saved into the script.
snippetenvsecret-text: Not stored — you will be asked again next time.
snippetenvdetected-text: The script reads this value from the environment.
playbookssubtitle-text: Describe what an instance should look like and apply it to any instance, as often as you like.
playbooksemptybody-text: A playbook lists packages, users, files, services and commands in cloud-config's vocabulary, or is an Ansible playbook. Applying one changes only what differs, so it can be run again and again.
playbooknameinvalid-text: Names may contain letters, digits, dots, underscores and dashes.
playbooknametaken-text: A playbook with this name already exists.
playbookyamlinvalid-text: The playbook is not valid YAML: %s
playbookshape-text: A playbook is a YAML mapping with cloud-config keys, or a list of Ansible plays.
playbooknotplay-text: Every entry of an Ansible playbook is a play with a "hosts" key.
playbooknothing-text: Nothing to apply: none of the keys are ones the built-in engine handles (%s).
deleteplaybookbody-text: Instances it was applied to stay as they are.
applyplaybooknoinstances-text: There is no instance to apply the playbook to.
applyplaybookcheck-text: Check only: report what would change without changing anything
applyplaybooknosteps-text: This playbook has no steps to run: every switch is off and every list is empty.
playbooknorun-text: Not applied to any instance yet.
playbookfailedat-text: Step "%s" failed; the steps after it were not run.
nothingmounted-text: Nothing is currently mounted through this app.
mountlanding-text: The disk appears in every instance under /mnt/wsl/.
templatesdeprecatedinfo-text: Distro packages do the same job in the official WSL format — a package installs on any machine with WSL, not just through this app. Templates will be removed or merged into distro packages in a future release.
ai-models-failed-text: Could not load the model list.
ai-test-failed-text: The test request failed. Check the endpoint, key and model.
mcp-quickconnect-hint-text: Adds this server to Claude Desktop's configuration, bridged through npx mcp-remote (needs Node.js). Restart Claude Desktop afterwards.
mcp-quickconnect-done-text: Added to Claude Desktop — restart it to load the server.
mcp-quickconnect-notfound-text: Claude Desktop was not found on this machine.
mcp-quickconnect-failed-text: Could not update Claude Desktop's configuration.
sandbox-subtitle-text: An isolated instance an AI chat is confined to — the model can act only inside it, never on your own machine or other instances. Note: the sandbox itself still has normal internet access.
sandbox-chat-scope-text: This chat is confined to the sandbox. It can run commands and edit files inside this instance only — never your own machine or other instances. The sandbox itself still has normal internet access.
sandbox-chat-hint-text: Ask the assistant to set up or run something inside the sandbox.
sandbox-disk-space-text: Not enough free disk space — a sandbox needs about 3 GB.
vmcreateinfo-text: VMs run natively through Apple's Virtualization framework. Starting a VM opens a window with its display.
vmcloudimageplaceholder-text: Choose a cloud image to download, or enter a local disk image path
vmcloudimagehint-text: Boots straight into a ready-to-use system that is reachable over SSH. A local .raw, .img or .qcow2 file works too, e.g. an exported template.
vminstallerisohint-text: The VM window walks you through a normal install. The guest is not reachable until the install is finished.
vmrestoreimagehint-text: Leave empty to download the latest supported version automatically (several GB).
vmmacosrequiresapplesilicon-text: macOS guests require an Apple Silicon Mac.
web-buy-detail-text: Buy once on wslmanager.com and unlock all Pro features — AI Workspace agents, AI Chat (with your own API key), Error Diagnosis and the MCP server. No subscription, free updates.
win-web-buy-detail-text: Buy a licence key once on wslmanager.com instead and activate it below. Same Pro features, no Microsoft account and no Store needed — handy for offline or managed machines. No subscription, free updates.
win-activate-detail-text: Paste the key from your website purchase to unlock Pro on this computer. A Microsoft Store copy needs no key — it unlocks itself.
win-activate-free-detail-text: Paste the key from your website purchase to unlock Pro on this computer. Bought Pro in the Microsoft Store while it was still a paid app? That copy unlocks itself, even after a reinstall, as long as this PC is signed in to the Microsoft Store with the account that bought it — if it does not, use “Get help” below and we will send you a key.
plan-free-detail-vm: Everything for managing virtual machines locally. AI features are not included.
vmstoppedimmediately-text: The VM stopped right after starting — most likely nothing bootable was found. Attach an installer ISO or create the VM from a base disk image.
templatesinfo-vm-text: A template is a saved VM disk image you can stamp new VMs from. Save one with the archive button in a VM row on Home.
vmisoplaceholder-text: Choose an installer to download, or enter a local ISO path
vmmacosterminaldenied-text: %s0 refused the app's SSH key for the account "%s1", and a macOS guest has no serial console to fall back on. Check that the account exists in the guest and that Remote Login is on (System Settings → General → Sharing), or name the right account in the VM's login details.
vmmacosterminalunreachable-text: %s0 cannot be reached over SSH, and a macOS guest has no serial console to fall back on. Open its screen and turn Remote Login on (System Settings → General → Sharing). %s1
vmgreeting-info-text: Show a system summary with fastfetch whenever a VM terminal or its login prompt opens. Installs a small profile script in the guest and fetches fastfetch through the guest's own package manager when it is missing.
vmdiskinuse-text: The VM is running, so its disk cannot be mounted — opening the VM folder instead.
vmdisknotmountable-text: macOS cannot read this disk's filesystem (Linux disks are usually ext4) — opening the VM folder instead.
vmejectbeforestart-text: This VM's disk is mounted in Finder. Eject it first, then start the VM.
listfailed-vm-text: The list of virtual machines could not be read.
listfailedhint-vm-text: The vmctl helper could not be reached. In a release build it ships inside the app; in a development run, execute scripts/build_macos.sh once to install it, then try again.
ai-workspace-vm-missing-text: The AI Workspace needs a Linux VM named 'ai-workspace'. Create one (a cloud image or an installed Linux VM) on the Home screen, then reopen this page.
ai-workspace-vm-stopped-text: The 'ai-workspace' VM exists but is not running. Start it from the Home screen, then try again.
vmbootsourcerequired-text: Choose a cloud image or an installer ISO — a VM with neither has nothing to boot and stops immediately.
vmcreatedwithservice-text: VM %s created. %s installs the first time it runs.
vmcreatelookup-text: Looking up the latest macOS restore image…
installservicefailed-text: Could not install the service in %s: %s
ai-workspace-setup-text: The AI Workspace runs in its own Linux VM ('ai-workspace'). Set it up automatically: this downloads Debian (about 3 GB, reused if cached), creates the VM and starts it — a few minutes on first run.
ai-workspace-vm-unreachable-text: The workspace VM did not become reachable over SSH. Check its console from the Home screen, then try again.
communitysnippetssubtitle-text: Ready-made scripts shared by the community. Pick the ones you want and they are added to your snippets.
ai-workspace-repair-text: The 'ai-workspace' VM is running but does not answer over SSH. Repair restarts it with a fresh network setup; nothing on its disk is lost.
ai-workspace-start-vm-text: The 'ai-workspace' VM exists but is stopped. Start it to continue.
ai-workspace-repairing-text: Repairing the workspace VM's network setup…
snippeteditorsubtitle-text: These fields are the ones the community repo expects, so a snippet can be shared as a pull request without rewriting anything.
snippetnameinvalid-text: Use only letters, numbers, dots, dashes and underscores — the name becomes a folder in the scripts repo.
sharesnippetbody-text: This opens a pull request on the wsl-scripts repository adding "%s" as info.yml and script.noshell. You sign in to GitHub once; the app never sees your password.
githubentercode-text: Enter this code in the browser window that just opened:
githubcodecopied-text: The code was copied to your clipboard.
pullrequestcreated-text: Pull request created. Thank you for sharing!
githubsignintimeout-text: The sign-in code expired before it was used. Try again.
githubnotconfigured-text: Sharing needs a GitHub OAuth client id, which this build was compiled without. See the contributing docs for how to add one.
activate-detail-text: Paste the key from your purchase to unlock Pro on this Mac. Buying on the website hands it over automatically.
activate-invalid-text: That licence key was not accepted. Check it for typos, or get in touch.
activate-network-text: Could not reach the licence service. Check your connection and try again.
plan-key-detail: Activated with a licence key from wslmanager.com. All Pro features are unlocked, updates included.
web-dashboard-info-text: Host a browser dashboard for this app that you can open from your phone or any other device on the same network: see, start, stop and manage your instances, run commands, open terminals and use every tool the app offers. Optionally publish it beyond your network through a Cloudflare tunnel.
web-dashboard-pro-required-text: The web dashboard is a Pro feature.
web-dashboard-toggle-hint-text: Starts a web server on port 59134 that other devices on your network can reach. Every request must carry the access token that is part of the link below.
web-dashboard-start-failed-text: The web dashboard could not be started. Is port 59134 already in use?
web-dashboard-url-hint-text: Pick the address the other device can reach, then scan the QR code with your phone or copy the link. The token is included.
web-dashboard-no-network-text: No network address found — only this machine can reach the dashboard right now.
web-dashboard-token-hint-text: The token is part of every link and QR code. Regenerating it invalidates all of them.
web-dashboard-tunnel-toggle-hint-text: Creates a temporary public HTTPS address (via Cloudflare) so the dashboard also works away from your network.
web-dashboard-tunnel-warning-text: The dashboard — including running commands and deleting instances — is now reachable from the public internet. Only the access token in the link protects it. Share the link only with people you trust.
web-dashboard-feature: Web dashboard for phones and other devices
guestaccessbody-text: Snippets run inside the VM over SSH, but this VM does not accept the app's key yet — VMs installed by hand from an ISO are not provisioned automatically. Sign in once with a guest account: the app's public key is added to that account and to root, and the password is used for this sign-in only and not stored.
guestaccessinstalling-text: Installing the app's SSH key in the VM…
guestaccessempty-text: Enter a user name and password.
guestaccessdone-text: SSH access to %s is set up.
guestaccessstilldenied-text: The key is installed, but %s1 refuses SSH both as %s0 and as %s2. Set the right account in the VM's login details, or allow root login by key in the guest's sshd config.
guestaccessadopted-text: %s0 is now reached as "%s1": that account accepts the key, while "%s2" is still refused. Change it any time in the VM's login details.
about-tagline: Manage WSL distributions and Linux VMs from one place.
about-dependencies-desc: Open-source libraries this app is built on
about-license-desc: Terms this app is distributed under
update-store-managed-text: The Microsoft Store keeps this installation up to date.
update-uptodate-text: You are running the latest version.
update-detail-text: The app closes while the update is installed and starts again afterwards.
update-manual-text: This release has no installer for your system. Download it from the release page.
update-failed-text: The update could not be downloaded. Please try again later.
update-failed-extract-text: The downloaded update could not be unpacked.
createinstanceinfo-text: Name the instance and choose what it is created from — a distro image, a Docker image or a local file.
containersinfo-text: Docker and Podman containers on this machine. Your container engine owns them; WSL Manager shows and drives them.
containerenginefailed-text: The container engine did not answer
nocontainerenginehint-text: Install Docker or Podman, make sure its command is on your PATH, then refresh.
nocontainershint-text: Containers you create with Docker or Podman show up here.
nologs-text: This container has not logged anything.
deletecontainerbody-text: This removes the container and everything written inside it that is not stored in a volume. The image it was created from is kept.
containerenginehint-text: Which engine the Containers screen and the AI tools drive. Automatic uses Docker when it is installed, otherwise Podman.
vmlogindetailsbody-text: The app signs in with its SSH key, so it never asks for these. The VM's own screen and serial console do: this is the account and password to type at their login prompt.
vmloginnopassword-text: The app keeps no login password for this VM: a root-only Linux guest needs none, and a macOS guest uses the account you set up on its first boot.
vmloginpending-text: This VM was created before it could be given a password. One has been set now and takes effect the next time the VM boots.
vmloginuserhint-text: Every SSH path into this VM signs in as this account — the terminal button, snippets, playbooks. A macOS guest keeps the name you typed into Setup Assistant, which the app never sees, so correct it here.
vminvaliduser-text: Use a lower-case Linux account name: letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter or _.
windowsterminal-info-text: Your instances can show up in the Windows Terminal dropdown, next to the profiles it creates itself. They are contributed through %s, a file of this app's own — your Windows Terminal settings are never edited.
windowsterminalsyncinfo-text: The list is kept up to date while the app runs, so an instance you create today is in the menu tomorrow.
windowsterminalhidegeneratedinfo-text: Windows Terminal lists every WSL distro by itself. Leave this on unless you want two entries per distro.
windowsterminalrestart-text: Windows Terminal reads the list when it starts, so open a new window to see the change.
windowsterminalunchanged-text: Windows Terminal already lists the same instances.
windowsterminalcleared-text: This app's profiles were removed from Windows Terminal.
windowsterminalfailed-text: Could not write the Windows Terminal profiles. %s
windowsterminalunsupported-text: Windows Terminal profiles can only be written for instances running on this machine.
kubernetesinfo-text: Workloads in the clusters your kubeconfig knows about. The cluster owns them; WSL Manager reads and drives them through kubectl.
nokubectlhint-text: Install kubectl, make sure its command is on your PATH, then refresh.
nokubecontexthint-text: Add a cluster to ~/.kube/config, or point WSL Manager at a kubeconfig file in the settings, then refresh.
noworkloadshint-text: Deployments, StatefulSets and DaemonSets of the selected namespace show up here.
noworkloadmatchhint-text: The filter matches names, namespaces and images. Clear it to see everything again.
nodetails-text: The cluster returned no details for this workload.
scalebody-text: How many replicas should run? The cluster starts or stops pods until it matches.
scaleinvalid-text: Enter a whole number of replicas, 0 or more.
nopods-text: This workload has no pods right now.
nopodlogs-text: This pod has not logged anything.
restartpodbody-text: The pod is deleted and its controller starts a replacement. Anything it kept outside a volume is lost.
kubeconfighint-text: Empty uses KUBECONFIG, or ~/.kube/config when that is unset. Point this at a file to work from another kubeconfig.
cloudinfo-text: Servers at your cloud provider. Deploy an instance onto a new one, or pull it back to this machine.
cloudconnectinfo-text: WSL Manager talks to your provider with an API token you create yourself. The token is stored on this machine only.
cloudtokenhint-text: Create a read & write token under Security in your project at %s. It is shown only once there, so paste it now.
cloudtokenmissing-text: Please paste an API token first.
clouddisconnectbody-text: The API token is removed from this machine. Your servers keep running and are not touched.
cloudproviderfailed-text: The cloud provider did not answer
nocloudservershint-text: Deploy an instance to create your first server, or create one in your provider console and refresh.
clouddeployinfo-text: The instance's root filesystem is exported, uploaded to a new server and started there as a container. Nothing local is changed.
clouddeploywarning-text: The server is billed from the moment it is created until you delete it.
clouddeployincomplete-text: Choose a size, a location and a base image.
clouddeploynotsupported-text: This backend cannot export an instance as a root filesystem, so it cannot be deployed.
clouddeploynoinstances-text: There is no instance to deploy yet.
cloudinvalidname-text: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or a digit.
cloudpullbody-text: %s is exported on the server and imported here as a new instance. The server keeps running.
cloudpullname-text: Name for the new local instance
clouddeletebody-text: The server and its disk are deleted at the provider and billing stops. Anything on it you did not pull back is gone.
cloudstage-waitingforserver-text: Waiting for the server to boot
cloudstage-waitingfordocker-text: Waiting for the server to finish setting up
vmrootfsnotfound-text: There is no VM named %s on this machine.
vmrootfsmacosguest-text: %s is a macOS guest. Only Linux VMs can be moved as a root filesystem.
vmrootfsunreachable-text: Could not reach %s over SSH, so its root filesystem cannot be read.
vmrootfsexportfailed-text: Could not read the root filesystem of %s.
vmrootfsempty-text: %s handed back an empty root filesystem.
vmrootfsnosource-text: This backend restores into a copy of the VM the deploy came from, and none was named.
vmrootfssourcemissing-text: %s is no longer on this machine. Its disk is needed as the base to restore onto, because a root filesystem on its own carries no kernel to boot.
vmrootfssourcerunning-text: Stop %s first. Its disk is copied as the base for the restore, and it cannot be copied while it runs.
vmrootfsrestorefailed-text: Could not restore the root filesystem into %s.
cloudpullbodyclone-text: %s is exported on the server and restored here into a copy of the local VM it was deployed from. That VM has to exist and be stopped; it is not changed, and the server keeps running.
cloudinitsubtitle-text: Saved cloud-init configurations. Pick one when adding an instance and it runs on the first boot: packages, users, files, commands.
cloudinitemptybody-text: Create one and choose it on the Add instance page. Cloud images on macOS and Ubuntu 24.04 or later on WSL apply it on their first boot.
cloudinitnamerequired-text: Enter a name for the configuration.
cloudinitnameinvalid-text: Use letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores only.
cloudinitnametaken-text: A configuration with this name already exists.
cloudinitheaderinvalid-text: cloud-init user-data has to start with #cloud-config (YAML) or #! (a script).
cloudinityamlnotamap-text: A #cloud-config document has to be a YAML mapping of keys to values.
deletecloudinitbody-text: This removes the configuration from this app. Instances already created with it are not changed.
cloudinitwslhint-text: Runs on the first start of distros that ship cloud-init, such as Ubuntu 24.04 and later; other distros ignore it.
cloudinitvmhint-text: Runs on the first boot of a cloud image, next to the account and SSH key the app sets up.
cloudinitfileexists-text: A cloud-init file for this name already exists: %s. Remove it or pick another name.
cloudinitfilewritefailed-text: Could not write the cloud-init file: %s
cloudinitmissing-text: The cloud-init configuration %s no longer exists.
cloudinitwaiting-text: Waiting for cloud-init to finish in %s...
cloudinitwaitfailed-text: Could not confirm that cloud-init finished in %s. Check "cloud-init status" inside the instance; the configuration file stays in place for its first start.
cloudinitnotrun-text: %s does not run cloud-init, so the configuration was not applied.
cloudinitunsupported-text: Cloud-init configurations are not available for this instance backend.
ai-workspace-shared-subtitle: Every tool uses the assistant's API endpoint, key and model from Settings under 'Bring Your Own AI Key'. Set them there once: installed tools are configured with them, and a tool installed later gets them too.
ai-workspace-shared-unset-text: Not set up yet. Add the assistant's API endpoint, key and model in Settings under 'Bring Your Own AI Key'; every tool will use them.
ai-workspace-shared-required-text: An endpoint and a model are required.
ai-workspace-shared-invalid-text: The assistant's endpoint, model and key must not contain spaces or quotes. Change them in Settings.
ai-workspace-shared-tools-updated-text: Every installed tool now uses the assistant's model and endpoint.
ai-workspace-shared-none-installed-text: No tool is installed yet. Each tool gets the assistant's settings as it is installed.
ai-workspace-shared-restart-hint-text: A tool that is running picks up the change after a restart.
ai-workspace-shared-openwebui-text: Open WebUI takes its endpoint from the container it was created with. Set it in its own admin panel under Connections.
ai-workspace-shared-no-output-text: The tool reported no error message.
ai-workspace-shared-auto-applied-text: %s was set up with the assistant's model and endpoint.
ai-workspace-shared-auto-failed-text: %s0 could not take the assistant's model and endpoint: %s1
experimentalfeatures-info-text: Features that are not finished yet. Each one stays hidden until you switch it on here; it then appears in the navigation and, where it has them, in the assistant's tools and in Settings.
experimental-containers-info-text: Manage the Docker and Podman containers on this machine.
experimental-kubernetes-info-text: Browse the clusters from your kubeconfig.
experimental-cloud-info-text: Deploy an instance to a cloud provider and pull it back.
experimental-cloudinit-info-text: Write cloud-init configurations and seed new instances with them.
experimental-playbooks-info-text: Describe an instance's state as code and apply it to existing instances.
wslversionsinfo-text: Which WSL version each installed distro runs on, and which version new distros are created with.
defaultwslversioninfo-text: New distros are created with this version. Distros that already exist are not changed.
defaultwslversionset-text: New distros will be created as WSL %s.
defaultwslversionfailed-text: Could not set the default WSL version. %s
convertwslversionbody-text: This rewrites the whole disk and can take several minutes. The distro is shut down first and cannot be used until the conversion finishes.
wslversionsunavailable-text: wsl.exe did not report any versions. %s
vmresizebody-text: How much machine this VM gets. The VM has to be stopped, and the new values are used the next time it starts.
vmresizecurrent-text: Now: %s0 cores, %s1 GB memory, %s2 GB disk. This Mac has %s3 cores.
vmresizerunning-text: The VM is running. Stop it first — its hardware is fixed for as long as it runs.
vmresizeshrink-text: A disk can only grow. Making it smaller would cut through the partitions the guest put at the end of it.
vmresizepositive-text: Enter a whole number greater than zero in each box.
vmresizenochange-text: These are the values the VM already has.
vmresizeunknown-text: This VM could not be found.
vmresizeguestgrows-text: A bigger disk reaches the guest as a bigger block device; this Linux guest grows its own root filesystem to fill it while it boots.
vmresizeguestmanual-text: A bigger disk reaches the guest as a bigger block device, but the guest keeps the filesystem it has. Grow it from inside the guest — Disk Utility on macOS, growpart and resize2fs on Linux.
vmresized-text: %s0 now has %s1 cores, %s2 GB memory and a %s3 GB disk. It takes effect on the next start.
